body:
the whole album turns on a single thread.

when taylor announced folklore, she described it as songs about "a single thread that, for better or for worse, ties you to your fate." "invisible string" is that idea made literal -- years of near-misses and wrong turns reeled back to one green afternoon reading in the grass at nashville's centennial park. "green was the color of the grass where i used to read at centennial park."

on a record full of invented characters -- the teenage love triangle, the widow, the ghost -- this is the one everybody treats as the plainly happy autobiographical song. the rare folklore track where the string doesn't fray. where fate, for once, just holds.

npr put it at no. 22 on its best songs of 2020. but it's the image itself we keep coming back to: one thread, running quietly through a whole life, pulling everything toward where it was always going.

longlivets.com
